claims.statement: When an H.264 bitstream carries no bit_rate_value_minus1 (i.e. no explicit HRD bit rate), BitRate is inferred as 1000 * MaxBR (VCL) / 1200 * MaxBR (NAL) for profile_idc 66, 77 or 88 (Baseline/Constrained Baseline, Main, Extended) and as cpbBrVclFactor * MaxBR / cpbBrNalFactor * MaxBR for other profiles; CpbSize is inferred the same way from MaxCPB. Level conformance is therefore evaluated against an HRD running at the level ceiling, not against the encoder's target bitrate.

design_risks: Level default 4.0 vs 1080p50/60: any 1080p50/60 encode exceeds Level 4.0/4.1 MaxMBPS (L-14) and needs Level 4.2 set explicitly (control h264_level=13 or caps level=(string)4.2); leaving the default (register D-12) is reported to fail at 1440x1080@50 (L-33).

Real-time headroom above Level 4.0 is not guaranteed by Raspberry Pi: the driver itself warns levels above 4.0 'may not be able to keep up with real-time' (L-28); a 1080p60 encode plus a second concurrent encode may exceed the single H.264 block's capacity (L-29..L-31).

Two encodes (recording + live) share one H.264 block and the ISP; the kernel will happily create both contexts (no limit, L-25/L-26) so overload shows up as dropped/late frames, not as an open() error.

25 Mbit/s equals exactly the High Level 4.0 VCL MaxBR (L-12): a 25 Mbit/s recording signalled at Level 4.0 has zero bitrate margin; signal Level 4.1/4.2 for the recording stream. 17 Mbit/s CBR at Constrained Baseline/Main Level 4.0 uses 85% of MaxBR (L-13).

Network: 102 Mbit/s of video payload alone (5 WebRTC + 1 RTMP at 17 Mbit/s, L-22) is ~10% of a Gigabit link but would exceed a link that negotiates 100 Mbit/s; no official Pi 4/CM4 Ethernet throughput figure exists (L-21), so egress capacity must be measured.
GStreamer extra-controls silently ignores misspelt control names (GST_WARNING only, L-55); test scripts must verify applied values with 'v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video11 -C ...' or GST_DEBUG=v4l2*:5.

Caps-specified profile/level override extra-controls, and on GStreamer main an auto-calculated level overrides extra-controls when caps do not fix a level (L-62): set profile/level in caps as well as (or instead of) extra-controls.
Writing h264_i_frame_period also writes video_gop_size on bcm2835-codec (L-57); setting both with different values in one extra-controls structure gives an order-dependent result.

FFmpeg h264_v4l2m2m sets no H264_LEVEL or BITRATE_MODE (L-43), so an FFmpeg-based 1080p50/60 test runs at the driver's default level 4.0 and default bitrate mode — use GStreamer or v4l2-ctl for level-4.2 tests, or set the level beforehand with v4l2-ctl (persistence across file handles is NOT expected because controls are per-open context, L-23).
